text.p: Finnish oil and energy group Neste Oy said on Friday weak petrochemicals and a significant loss on crude oil trading knocked it into the red in January-August, but it forecast a profit for the full year.

Reporting a loss before extraordinaries and tax of 26 million markka ($5.7 million) from a 1.14 billion markka profit in the year-ago period, Neste said the result was also hit by lower gains on the sale of fixed assets.

"We can anticipate that Neste's performance during the last four months of the year will improve, and that the group's overall result before extraordinary items for 1996 will be profitable, albeit substantially poorer than in 1995," Neste said in a statement with the results.

Per share in January-August it made a 2.61 markka loss against a 6.63 markka profit last year. Net sales fell to 27.65 billion from 29.91 billion. At the operating level it made a profit of 341 million markka against 1.71 billion.
The median of analysts' forecasts had been for a 295 million markka profit after financial items; none forecast a loss.
Neste said its oil division had incurred an 81 million markka operating loss.
"The loss for the oil division includes a sales margin deficit of 495 million markka posted by Neste's crude oil trading," Neste said.

"This sum includes losses realised by the end of the review period as well as potential losses on commitments due within the next 12 months market-to-market at the time the interim report was being prepared," it said.
In 1995, Neste's profit before extras and tax was 1.36 billion markka. ($ = 4.574 Finnish Markka)
